summary:
We developed "Artemis Calling," a three-level interactive educational game inspired by NASA's Artemis program and starring a character named Star. The project tackles both the technical challenges of space engineering and social barriers through a progressive three-level experience:

• Simulation and Decision-Making (Level 1): In Star’s bedroom (making stops at the refrigerator, desk, closet, and toy box), players must make real engineering and resource management decisions based on NASA guidelines. Each correct choice earns points toward launch, while a mistake forces them to rethink the mission.

• Space Education and Curiosity (Level 2): During the spaceflight, participants answer general knowledge questions about space in order to successfully land on the Moon, encouraging active learning.

• Access to Real Opportunities (Level 3): Upon reaching the Moon, the game unlocks direct links with information about the first female astronaut, global NASA competitions, and internship or job programs.

Our solution is important because it has the potential to bring space knowledge closer to many girls around the world, breaking down gender and socioeconomic stereotypes, as our game is designed to be playable on any computer. Artemis Calling shows girls that working at NASA is within their reach and gives them real tools to achieve it, motivating them to create, explore, and fulfill their dreams.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?
The game works across three levels where the main character, named Star, guides each girl through planning, active learning about space, and landing on the Moon as the main goal. Inspired by the Artemis program, the game features questions that help Star design her space mission to the Moon, where players find valuable resources that motivate girls to learn more about NASA, female astronauts, and the opportunity to achieve their dreams.

What benefits does it offer?

  • Educational: Girls have the opportunity to learn more about missions like the Moon landing, interesting facts about space, and other information that can help them make important decisions about their future.
  • Social: It helps reduce both the gender gap and the social gap in STEAM activities, encouraging more girls to feel motivated to work at NASA as scientists or astronauts.
  • Real opportunities: At the end of the game, when girls reach "the Moon," they can access valuable information for their future, motivating them to aspire to become astronauts like Sally Ride or scientists involved in NASA projects through job opportunities or internships.

What is the intended impact of the project?
To provide girls around the world—regardless of their economic or social conditions—with the opportunity to aspire to work at NASA and continue writing space history. In the long term, we hope that through our game, more girls will become interested in space, science, and technology.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?
Our game was developed using the C++ programming language and the raylib graphics library. Some of the images were downloaded from Google, while other illustrations were created in IbisPaint. It is a standalone executable file (.exe) to ensure it can run on as many types of computers as possible, making the game accessible to low-income girls who do not have access to high-end technology, Furthermore, our application was designed so that, for each mission attempt, the questions are randomized; correct answers are removed, and questions that have already been answered do not reappear—ensuring that every session is different, Ultimately, the code was written manually; we did not use SI.

In what way is your project creative?
We consider our project creative because it combines technology, science-based decision-making for a real space mission, curiosity, competitiveness, information, and real opportunities for girls globally. Our game successfully blends the best of the scientific world and fun to create an experience capable of inspiring girls and reducing gender stereotypes surrounding becoming an astronaut or working at NASA, Furthermore, our project is open source, so anyone can modify it and create their own mods.

What factors did your team consider?

  • The need to fulfill the design of a space mission through our game.
  • The opportunity for our game to go beyond just solving the NASA challenge, helping to reduce a real social challenge and stereotype.
  • The reality that many girls who dream of becoming astronauts lack the financial resources to even access information that brings them closer to their dream, which is why our game is built in a lightweight format compatible with most computers.
  • The combination of science and fun, since our game uses real scientific data within an interactive experience that ultimately provides information to support the future decisions of girls around the world.
